rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods / Tables 1-2 / Fig. 6 - two-year field experiment (2003, 2006) at Harran University farm comparing water pillow irrigation at three levels with furrow irrigation for soybean, with own yield, soil water, ET and soil temperature measurements.
rows.notes: The study tests the water pillow (WP) method, a perforated black polyethylene pipe laid on the soil surface that trickles water by gravity, compared with furrow irrigation; it is not drip irrigation under plastic mulch. The study does report its own results that WP plots had higher pre-irrigation soil water content (Section 3.1) and higher soil temperature at 20 cm, about 1.4-2.0 C warmer than furrow (Section 3.3, Fig. 6), but no nutrient availability data. Because the technology is a related but different system (explicitly the water-pillow case), Q2 is answered no and technology_mismatch is set.
